text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000194's 99215 rate is elevated in every complexity band, including patients with no chronic conditions, yet the few charts returned support every billed 99215, so the evidence is mixed.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern points toward upcoding: the excess 99215 share appears even among patients with zero or one chronic condition, and the low-complexity samples (e.g., C0097770 for low back pain, C0097773 and C0097909 for UTI, C0097907 for an upper respiratory infection with hyperlipidemia) look like routine problems. The documentation points the other way, since none of the documented 99215 claims fell below the billed level, but only 9 such charts came back, which is too few to rule out inflation. Two of the supported charts, C0097909 and C0097907, record high MDM and long visit times for low-complexity encounters, and a few notes claim moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim. Both points are weak signs that notes may be templated or inflated to match the billed level, not proof. A reviewer should first pull and read the full notes for C0097907 and C0097909 and the other low-complexity 99215 claims, checking whether the MDM narrative and time are specific to the visit or cloned. A reviewer should then request a larger chart sample, including the heavy 99214 volume."}
